summary: Bounding the remote poller to 1,024 transcript items permanently cuts off older TUI chat scrollback because PendingPrefix only converts the supplied snapshot and never fetches omitted SQLite rows.

Passing the 1,024-item truncated transcript to PreparedMaterializedSessionDetail::from_materialized drops unread agent message and session restart ordinals that fall before the window and overwrites startup summary counts.

When a single turn exceeds 1,024 transcript items, the latest user prompt falls outside the polled tail, causing PreparedMaterializedSessionDetail::from_materialized to clear the dashboard 'You:' excerpt and suppress latest_agent_activity_after_last_user.
load_materialized_projection_tail_from runs an O(N) COUNT(*) over all transcript rows for the session on every poll and resume seed even though omitted_items is unused in production.

load_materialized_projection_tail_from computes latest_user_position via last_materialized_user_message, which skips empty or image-only user messages unlike ProjectionWindow::of and latest_completed_turn_ordinal.
Claim that raw_only entries in the 1,024-item polled tail cause the browser transcript to drop visible lines or appear empty.
Claim that TurnReviewHost receives the 1,024-item truncated projection from the poller and loses the original task in seed_from_session.
When a session exceeds 1,024 items, each newly appended item evicts the front of the polled tail and shifts a scrolled-up chat's index-based TranscriptAnchor::Row forward.

first_materialized_user_message restricts SQL matching to stable_id GLOB 'user:*' or 'user-*', skipping valid restored canonical user items with other stable IDs and potentially clearing their provisional title.
The new unit test a_windowed_projection_answers_the_same_title_and_turn_as_a_whole_one slices whole.transcript[3..], which still includes the latest user message contrary to its comment.
Claim that ProjectionWindow::of repeats expensive provisional_title computation on every StandaloneSession::snapshot even when session_title is already set.
Deleting embedded_npm_recipes_match_the_runtime_pins removes the only automated check that embedded Codex and Claude package.json files stay synchronized with mj-core's runtime version pins.
Deleting a_harness_restart_gates_dispatch_until_the_session_is_configured_again removes the only regression test covering the HarnessRestarting-to-SessionConfigured dispatch gate.

Deleting daemon_restart_without_a_baseline_does_not_hide_pending_work removes the only worker-startup test verifying that restarting an existing relay without a review baseline does not create a new one.

Deleting reviewer_fast_mode_is_applied_when_advertised_and_optional_otherwise removes the only worker test verifying that reviewer startup applies fast-mode=on when advertised and tolerates absence or rejection.
Deleting a_child_sends_its_report_as_a_handback_request removes the only socket test verifying child handback MCP request serialization and reply unwrapping.
Deleting a_wait_for_any_child_carries_return_when_and_the_harness_default removes the only socket assertion that wait forwards return_when: "any" and the Codex default timeout.
Deleting project_memory_connection_requests_round_trip_replica_and_baseline removes a direct in-process happy-path unit test of apply_project_memory_request.

Steering replaces active_turn with the queued prompt's ID so turn_started is emitted for the steered prompt, while the worker later completes the original command ID and emits turn_ended without an accepted ordinal, leaving the steered turn unclosed.
InputResolved takes turn_id from whichever turn is currently active at resolution time rather than the turn that requested the elicitation.
Provisional-session rollback deletes the session row and cascades api_events, causing record_api_error to skip persisting the launch failure so event subscribers never receive it.
Close-time checkpoint failures only update last_checkpoint_error and leave last_error unchanged, so the api_events triggers never emit an error event for a failed async close.
Adding the api_events and api_session_activity tables without advancing SCHEMA_VERSION lets an older daemon open and write the store without journaling events.
Optional OR predicates in load_api_events_from prevent SQLite from using the api_events_session(session_id, seq) index for session-filtered replay.
repair_projection resets the materialized projection without deduplicating api_events, so catch-up re-inserts previously projected events with new sequence numbers.
Activity recording runs only inside the optional phone server, leaving permanent gaps in activity_changed history whenever [phone].enabled is false or the server fails to start.
Racing record_activity_stream in run_server's top-level select! lets any auxiliary activity-write failure permanently tear down the phone and HTTP API server.
The viewer snapshot projection ignores relay connectivity health, so record_activity_stream never emits disconnect or reconnect activity_changed transitions.
Rejecting requests where after_seq and Last-Event-ID differ breaks normal SSE reconnection for clients that started with an after_seq query parameter.
Live-only SSE subscribers never receive the initial frontier sequence before the first matching event, so a disconnect before that event causes reconnects to miss events.
When a follow-only mj events stream terminates before any event arrives, the CLI error message advises resuming with --after-seq 0, which replays all skipped history.
stdout writes and flushes in mj events are awaited outside the ctrl_c() select after Tokio has installed its SIGINT handler, so Ctrl-C hangs when stdout is backpressured.
Unbounded usage_quota_row_count used as a fixed Length constraint can overflow the 20-row inline viewport and short fullscreen terminals, crowding out the input box or clipping wrapped quota text.
The new DeepSeek quota rendering test draws draw_usage_quota_row in isolation on a 5-row rect rather than testing the full inline or fullscreen layouts at constrained sizes.

Unconditionally wrapping all errors from resolve_local_repository in Refusal::precondition misclassifies Git execution, timeout, cancellation, and filesystem failures as 409 missing-remote refusals and drops the daemon-log reference.
When the capacity poller channel is closed, the 500 response directs callers to daemon-log reference `capacity-poller`, but no log entry records that reference.
LifecycleFailure::into_error rebuilds a refused error by wrapping the already-formatted full error chain around the Refusal, repeating the refusal sentence in subsequent `{error:#}` displays.
Claims missing-remote checks run only after the new session is accepted, so the Refusal cannot reach the caller.
A long or multiline recorded error in Confirmation::RecoverFailed can wrap beyond the terminal height and clip the explanation and action buttons off the bottom of the non-scrolling popup.

Choosing `Open transcript` on a failed (`SessionState::Error`) session fails with `session ... is not managed` because Error sessions are excluded from worker poll targets and have no live session-manager actor.
Requests adding a test that activates the default `Recover` button in Confirmation::RecoverFailed.
Answering a turn-review form spawns a new permanent polling loop for that role on top of its already-running loop.
Answered reviewer elicitations can be reopened or resubmitted before ElicitationResolved is projected, which fails the review on duplicate submission.
handle_mouse still prioritizes the underlying review split over an open reviewer elicitation dialog.
Metadata-only raw checkpoints still declare schema version 10, so older builds accept them, ignore review_refs_metadata_only, and fail or mutate checkouts.
collect_git_metadata_snapshot sets review_refs_metadata_only to false when no refs/mj/ refs exist, allowing restores with restore_contents=true to rewind or mutate the checkout.
Removing the destination-baseline refusal lets restore succeed with a foreign pin in place, which worker startup then overwrites in initialize_review_baselines, losing both sessions' baselines.
Submitting a prompt while a config update is in flight discards the prompt and leaves the UI permanently wedged in TurnState::Streaming.
refresh_config_picker retains numeric indices instead of option and value IDs, so reordering or removing options during a refresh can apply a different setting or value.
draw_config_picker_modal undercounts vertical chrome by one row, rendering an empty list for a single item and clipping one row for 2-8 items.
On terminals 8 rows tall or shorter, draw_config_picker_modal returns without drawing while config_picker remains open and continues capturing all keyboard input.

Cancelling a workspace close calls cancel_lifecycle on all originally active session IDs without checking operation ownership, which can abort an unrelated Resume started for an already-stopped session.
close_workspace checks its cancellation flag only before invoking close_session, so close_session continues stopping remaining children and the parent after cancellation is requested.
close_workspace does not guard against active non-in-place Move operations, allowing workspace deletion while the moving session is temporarily Stopped and breaking destination restoration.
close_workspace checks cancellation before queueing database::close_workspace on the serialized writer, so cancellation accepted while waiting for the writer does not stop workspace deletion.
When one dashboard closes the default workspace, other connected dashboards skip composer disposal in drain_runtime_state and retain drafts that reappear when a session is resumed.
discard_workspace_composers does not clear DashboardState::standby_prompts, so unsent standby text survives workspace closure and is restored when the session is later resumed.
If the post-close snapshot or workspace-list refresh fails in spawn_workspace_close, the committed close is reported as an error and explicit composer cleanup is skipped.
Cancelling a workspace close immediately after starting it can race ahead of close registration on the daemon, causing cancellation to fail while the close still runs.
workspace_close_finished ignores a reopened close dialog that is still loading, allowing its stale pre-deletion snapshot to open a fresh close confirmation for an already-deleted workspace.
Markdown link destinations are discarded in rich mode without creating clickable hyperlinks.
Header-only Markdown tables emit nothing when wider than the viewport.
Markdown table columns are joined without padding, so column separators do not align across rows.
Tight nested Markdown lists overwrite the parent item prefix and concatenate parent and child text onto one line.
Sanitizing streamed ACP chunks independently corrupts CRLF pairs and ANSI escape sequences split across chunk boundaries.
`wrap_styled_graphemes` silently drops the first wrapped row when wide characters have display width above `continuation_indent` but grapheme count at or below `continuation.len()`.
Tool call locations are not passed through `sanitize_terminal_text` before being stored and rendered in raw mode.
Multi-line list items lose their indentation after the first line because `finish_line` consumes `item_prefix`.
The new ignored Docker integration test starts `agent-dev:latest` and immediately asserts it has no baked worker, which fails once this commit's image is published.
Worker recovery and parked sub-agent wake still resolve and digest-compare a host worker, overwriting the image-worker symlink with a host copy.
Claims `.dockerignore` negations like `!mj-core/` exclude crate contents beneath those directories.
A dangling symlink at `/opt/mjolnir/mj-worker` is reported as `absent` because `[ -e ... ]` follows symlinks.
`scripts/build-agent-dev-image.sh` stamps uncommitted worker edits with the committed build ID and its warning check misses untracked source files.
`scripts/build-agent-dev-image.sh` imports `tomllib`, requiring Python 3.11+ without documenting or checking the requirement.
Uncommitted worker edits in a development build are silently ignored on container targets when the committed tree matches the image's worker build ID.
The local Podman build command in `mj-controller/docs/PODMAN.md` now fails because `Containerfile.agent-dev` requires worker build arguments.
DashboardState::show_close_failure has no production callers while the direct 'x' force-destroy shortcut was removed, leaving close recovery and force-destroy unreachable in the TUI.

Adding the cross-harness lossy label causes profile choices in the resume picker to wrap onto multiple lines, but render_picker sizes its popup by choice count without scrolling, clipping later selectable choices.
Streamed activity chunks still drop trailing spaces and join words across 3+ chunks because update_activity calls truncate_text (which collapses whitespace) on every append.
containers/Containerfile.agent-dev omits RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME from /etc/profile.d/20-mjolnir-tools.sh, breaking Rust toolchain discovery in agent-dev sessions under the clean login environment.
Worker login re-exec clears inherited and container-injected GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN before configure_github_cli (in Run) and !gh auth git-credential (in PushBranch) can read them.

Merging the cached login baseline via hel_login_environment::with_overrides in src/hel_acp.rs:870 (and supervisor launch) restores GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/GIT_CONFIG_KEY_* variables deliberately removed by configure_github_cli.
src/hel_terminal.rs:421 strips GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN after applying spawn.env, dropping tokens explicitly supplied in ACP terminal/create requests.

WorkerCommand::Diff and WorkerCommand::PushBranch re-exec with a clean environment without restoring target_environment, breaking targets that configure Git PATH, proxy, or SSH settings via target_environment.
Worker login re-exec clears SSH_AUTH_SOCK, breaking SSH-agent-authenticated Git operations on local and SSH-forwarded targets.
Worker login re-exec discards launcher XDG_CACHE_HOME, MJ_TEST_HOOK/MJ_TEST_HOOK_DIR, MJ_CHAOS_ISOLATED, and RUST_LOG that the e2e reliability and hook-chaos suites depend on.
Clean login re-exec discards Dockerfile ENV variables (such as PATH and MUSE_CLI) in custom container images built to the documented custom-image contract.
src/hel_login_environment.rs:169-170 invokes the user's account shell with ["-l", "-c", script], which fails on csh/tcsh where -l cannot be combined with -c.

src/hel_login_environment.rs executes pw_shell directly without handling non-interactive shells like /sbin/nologin or /bin/false, breaking custom container images whose user has a nologin passwd entry.
Changing user '!' shell execution from bash -lc to bash -c drops non-exported shell functions and bash login-file state.
scripts/run.sh now requires an undocumented node binary to parse Cargo's JSON output, failing only after building both workers on Rust-only setups.
docs/src/content/docs/custom-images.md still documents non-login worker shells and bash -lc for '!command', contradicting the new behavior.
Completed Progress entries in .agents/plans/clean-session-environment.md omit timestamps.

Re-hydrating a session via apply_worker_summary overwrites summarized_unread_agent_messages without pruning unread_agent_message_sequences, causing active_session_row to double-count live-polled unread messages after a reconnect.

Hydrating only a bounded transcript tail without setting last_agent_message or an all-history assistant flag lets Delete/Ctrl-D bypass confirmation and immediately destroy active sessions whose assistant replies precede the tail.
Upgrading a summary-hydrated worker to full history on open replays all events without notifying recovery_context, causing completed turns to miss automatic recovery checkpoints.

Exiting chat updates last_viewed_event_sequence without refreshing dashboard worker poll targets, so a later reconnect requests session_summary with a stale viewed_through cursor and restores unread badges for already-read messages.
The 'No messages yet' placeholder in active_transcript_tail is unreachable because both apply_transcript and apply_worker_summary store Some(transcript) even when the transcript is empty.

apply_worker_summary unconditionally overwrites current_turn_started_at and last_activity_at with observed_at_epoch_seconds on reconnect, resetting running-turn elapsed timers and bumping idle activity timestamps.

Full-history bootstrap on opening a summary-hydrated session runs synchronously inside run_dashboard's event loop with a per-page timeout, blocking key input and termination handling for potentially minutes.

ChatState::agent_message_start_sequences uses started_seq from the first chunk even if it was whitespace-only, causing summary unread counts to miss a message whose first nonblank text arrived after viewed_through.
DashboardState::set_state only clears summarized_unread_agent_messages when viewed_through reaches summarized_unread_through rather than decrementing on partial viewing.
apply_worker_summary does not suppress unread counts when the hydrated session is currently selected and expanded on the dashboard.
Switching ensure_models_installed to download only the four model files omits test_wavs/, causing the ignored dictation_models_install_and_decode_test_wav test to panic on a clean cache.

download_model_file uses a fixed .part temporary filename and unlinks it before downloading, allowing concurrent or restarted workers to rename an unfinished file into the final model path where has_model_data treats it as installed.
Interpolating the full per-file download status message before 'Ctrl-R stop' in the input block title causes narrow terminals to clip both the percentage and stop shortcut.
Removing extract_tar_bz2_file leaves bzip2 as an unused direct dependency in Cargo.toml.
busy_prompt_title takes precedence over dictation_prompt_title in draw_input, hiding dictation setup progress while an agent turn is streaming or cancelling.
dictation_prompt_title reads any StatusKind::Info status_line before microphone levels arrive, so unrelated user actions like Ctrl-Y overwrite the dictation loading status in the prompt title.
download_model_file formats file sizes using integer megabytes(), displaying '0 MB' for sub-megabyte model files like tokens.txt.
Recording launch failure directly in the runtime task races ahead of UiEvent::SessionStarted traversing the orchestrator channel, permanently marking a started session as a launch failure.
ServerSessionLaunchRegistry::begin evicts the oldest entry unconditionally even while it is still Starting, discarding its eventual failure if 64 newer launches occur.
serverLaunchFailure calls apiFetch without a timeout before refreshSessions() in the launch watch loop.
selectNewlyStartedSession does not recheck watcher ownership after awaiting serverLaunchFailure.
acp::run has no handshake timeout, so a live adapter that never answers initialize or session/new leaves the launch in Starting until the viewer times out.
Falling back to session/new after a failed session/load leaves session_updates_enabled false, silently dropping all session/update notifications for the replacement thread.

Snapshots written before this change default native_session_used to false without recovering prior SessionOpened { resumed: true } or imported-thread evidence, allowing an established conversation to be replaced.
native_session_may_have_history treats queued prompts removed before dispatch (RelayDispatchState::Rejected) as proof of native history, blocking empty-thread replacement.

A successful resume marks native_session_used in the durable relay but leaves the bridge's native_session_used atomic false, so an in-process bridge restart before a prompt or content update carries native_session_may_have_history = false to the next bridge.
Bare and raw-checkout bundle exports always fail with 'no commits beyond the session base' because their checkpoints omit committed history.
Bare-session file reads pass the parent of project_directory as --root, breaking relative paths and allowing reads of sibling directories and host files.
Session diffs for raw sessions opened in a repository subdirectory capture only that subdirectory into an empty index and report files outside it as deleted.
capture_worktree_tree uses an empty scratch index with git add -A, omitting tracked files matching ignore rules and reporting false deletions in session diffs.
Exported patches corrupt non-UTF-8 text files because diff_between_trees converts Git's output with String::from_utf8_lossy.
Unmanaged bare checkouts and existing linked worktrees supply neither --base nor --branch, so session diff always fails with 'no session base recorded'.
Standalone hel worker push-branch runs SystemGit without the session's synchronized GitHub credential environment, breaking HTTPS pushes on targets relying on it.
Leading-hyphen file paths or branch names fail Clap parsing with exit code 2 and are misreported as an outdated worker.
branch_creation_commit takes the oldest remaining reflog entry without checking whether the creation entry has expired, silently omitting earlier commits.
Live bundle export awaits checkpoint_session_now directly on the Axum/Tokio runtime thread instead of offloading synchronous subprocess work.
checkpoint_session_now does not reserve the session in RuntimeState.lifecycle, allowing concurrent API bundle checkpoints or lifecycle operations to race.
require_idle_turn treats a missing actor or snapshot as idle and checks only a cached snapshot, allowing push_branch to run during an active turn.
Bundle export treats stopped Podman sessions retaining target: Some(...) during deferred cleanup as live and attempts to checkpoint them instead of reading the saved archive.
Managed network workspace bundle exports exclude commits already pushed to origin because they reuse SessionDelta checkpoints.
plan_workspace_to_raw records the local repository's current HEAD as base_commit instead of the archived session base, causing diffs after move/resume to revert unrelated commits.
read_session_file has a TOCTOU window between path/size checks and fs::read, allowing concurrent workspace modifications to bypass root containment or the 16 MiB limit.
An overlapping checkpoint can prune the archive file returned by checkpoint_now before bundle export opens it for verification.
Metadata-only named_like scan sets preview: None without backfilling previews for matched rows, causing title/project-only search results to lose their fallback preview text.
cancel_component_pointer does not cancel ResumeDialog.preview_scrollbar, leaving an active thumb drag stuck capturing mouse and wheel events after FocusLost, Resize, or overlay interruption.
handle_resume_dialog_event returns without setting last_event_consumed when handle_resume_scrollbar_mouse consumes an event, skipping redraw before batched mouse events.
Preview hit buttons [↑] and [↓] accept keyboard focus via Tab/BackTab but render without any focus or pressed visual indicator.
ResumeDialog::prepare calls preview_body just to count hits, rebuilding and discarding the entire preview line list on every prepare call.
The width >= 30 threshold for rendering preview hit arrows does not leave enough room for 'Transcript · hit 1/10', causing [↑] to overwrite the hit count.
Preview hit arrows hardcode Unicode '↑' and '↓' instead of honoring ASCII mode via theme::glyphs().arrows_vertical.
Reviewer reported no findings on this commit.
Deferring a checkpoint exits before pack_checkpoint and leaks the uniquely named remote_stage directory created by prestage.
A deferred manual checkpoint persists last_checkpoint_error = None instead of restoring previous.last_checkpoint_error.
RecoveryCoordinator drops the retry of a deferred copy if the session's final Idle observation arrives before the deferred result is processed.
A harness-initiated turn during a close checkpoint's export/transfer causes HoldThroughClose to fail with CheckpointDeferred instead of waiting and retrying.
A self-started turn observed immediately after a prompt-driven turn overwrites prompt_driven in SessionWatch and skips the automatic review.
Coalescing the active-prompt Running view during a self-started turn causes Running(prompt_driven=false) -> Idle to skip automatic review.
installation_home adds synchronous std::fs::canonicalize calls to same_installation, which runs on the TUI event loop when applying profile discovery.
installation_home expands ~ when suppressing discovered absolute homes, but runtime consumers still use profile.home literally without tilde expansion.
When canonicalize fails for a missing target behind a symlink, the lexical fallback collapses symlink/.. and can falsely match and suppress a distinct discovered home.

When canonicalize fails due to a missing target or intermediate segment, the lexical fallback leaves symlinked ancestors (and Windows verbatim prefixes) unresolved, causing same_installation to miss equivalent homes.
Lexical fallback matches a configured path with a missing intermediate directory (missing/../home/.claude) to the existing /home/.claude.

same_installation now suppresses the discovered stock OpenCode/Muse profile when configured via a symlink or .., while is_own_nested_home still compares raw paths and selects the wrong data directory.

spawn_config_rename wraps both the daemon rename RPC and the post-save blocking Controller::load reload inside SAVE_ACK_TIMEOUT, so a slow reload causes a false daemon-acknowledgement timeout and discards the reload.

mark_session_import_complete treats any SessionStarted { resumed: true } as a completed replay, so adapters that support session/resume without session/load exit immediately with an empty handoff and discard the resumed session.

During the temporary import replay UI, user drafts are discarded on exit and prompts submitted before SessionStarted are sent to the temporary source runtime, cut off on Shutdown, and folded into the acknowledgement-only handoff as historical context.

Same-model fallback resumes are misclassified as cross-route imports when agent.reasoning_effort is configured because roster.available entries have reasoning_effort: None while roster.primary has the configured override.
Discarding the temporary UI transcript and showing the handoff placeholder in the new primary UI is the intended handoff design shared with TransferSession.
Dropping the picker's selected_role across SwitchSession and relying on session_provenance::find(&session_id, &cwd) with fallback to the active primary existed identically before this diff.

Cross-agent import handoffs omit mj-subagents.subagent_cancel tool results because AppState suppresses subagent transport calls from state.transcript and ACP replay does not repopulate state.nested_agents().
Changing image capability increments the shared input generation and silently discards in-flight text-only pastes in elicitation answers or history search.
ClipboardTarget::Answer only captures the elicitation request ID, so switching fields within a multi-field question during a clipboard read pastes into the newly focused field.
Attachment completion increments input_generation and cancels a concurrent clipboard read, but this behavior existed before this diff.
Matching Docker's 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon' error unconditionally classifies unreachable DOCKER_HOST or stale-context endpoints as NotRunning and advises starting Docker.
Reviewer reported no findings.

Upgrading or recovering a pre-existing macOS local Claude session with a linked profile home enables subagent_tools without installing mj-agents MCP config, disabling native Agent/Task tools while providing no replacement.
Legacy macOS Claude sessions with a non-default profile home are linked to the recorded harness_home rather than ~/.claude, which the earlier Claude process actually used.

Checkpointing a pre-upgrade local bare session before its launch.json is rewritten fails with 'project memory replica is outside the harness home' because starts_with does not resolve the profile symlink.
credential_sync_targets now performs a synchronous symlink_metadata filesystem check per local session directly on the TUI and web server event loops.

Legacy local bare sessions started by the earlier release always had installed_home created on disk by seed_local_memory_replica, and a missing harness_home already failed checkpointing before this diff.
docs/src/content/docs/profiles.md still documents the old behavior that raw local and macOS Claude sessions run directly from the user's profile home without staging.
When wait_for_session_start fails or times out after daemon admission, the session ID is already in self.sessions, causing unanswered_refusal() to return None and mj acp to exit with status 0.
Lab.cleanup() wraps the entire session-destroy loop in a single try/except, so one failed or timed-out destroy skips destroying all remaining sessions before stopping the daemon.
wait_for_session_start immediately aborts session/new on any transient connection error from look(), failing creation if a daemon restart or replacement overlaps a readiness poll.
wait_for_session_start waits for session.is_idle rather than prompt readiness, so a prompt held by another client during provisioning or background work can stall or time out session/new.
The completion assertion in tests/e2e/acp_real_harness.py checks only for the marker text without asserting that sessionUpdate is agent_message_chunk.
FakeDaemon::session_json derives is_idle directly from lifecycle, state, and chat_phase, so the unit test never covers a live/running/idle session with is_idle: false.
`mj go` fails on unbound directories named `default` (case-insensitively) when the legacy `default` workspace is empty because `go::available_workspace_name` does not reserve `default`.
Creating a workspace named `default` via `POST /api/v1/workspaces` when the legacy `default` row is empty returns HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 400.

`mj new` checks for `--workspace` only after reading the prompt (including stdin `-`) and validating `--bundle`/`--project-directory`, causing missing-workspace invocations to block on stdin or exit with the unrelated directory error.

The missing-workspace refusal displays `workspace.session_count`, which counts only active sessions and therefore prints `0 sessions` for a listed `default` workspace containing only suspended sessions.
Exposing the `default` workspace when it holds only suspended sessions allows deleting its `workspaces` row, which breaks `record_prompt_to` for all subsequent prompts in every workspace.

If a visible `default` workspace is renamed and its last session is later removed, it disappears from listings while `refuse_legacy_default_name` refuses to recreate a workspace with that renamed name.
`workspace_required` awaits `daemon.list_workspaces()` without an explicit client-side timeout.
`workspace_required` logs daemon connection or listing errors with `tracing::warn!` and omits the workspace list instead of surfacing the daemon error to the user.
The new test in `mj-cli/tests/acp.rs` calls `Command::output()` instead of a shared subprocess helper.
Combined background activity labels such as `1 task, 1 shell 50s` exceed the minimized Sessions pane status width and get right-truncated, hiding the elapsed clock.
open_checkpoint_relay drops a held Move relay lease before restarting an unreachable worker instead of keeping the lease and replacing its connection, reopening the session actor admission window.
prepare_move_source_checkpoint releases the adopted checkpoint-only lease when source_relay is empty, leaving the actor un-leased before the sealing checkpoint.
Retrying a Move after queue_admission_started skips drop(source_relay), holding the live destination actor's lease through workspace cleanup and queue replay.
move_session_managed_controlled holds the source session lease across validate_move_destination_configuration, which runs a fresh serialized profile probe.
Holding the session actor's connection does not prevent work already queued in the worker from starting before BeginCheckpoint.
Updated Move and checkpoint tests pass MoveSourceRelay::default() and do not add a new test exercising a held source relay.
owner_only_create_options declares `let mut options` even though the only mutation is under `#[cfg(unix)]`, triggering unused_mut and failing Windows Clippy with -D warnings.
Provisioning creates newly provisioned worker roots with mkdir -p / create_dir_all before the worker starts, so WorkerRootOwner::acquire's create_owner_only_directory leaves new worker roots at 0755.
Upgrading does not retroactively tighten permissions on pre-existing directories and active.jsonl files.
Partially clipped model and effort chips still render with clickable chip styling, but register no hitbox when their full width exceeds the border limit.
Clicking a model or effort chip leaves task_control_focused or subagent_control_focused set, so those controls intercept keyboard input before the open config picker.
Chip hitboxes do not reserve space for the right-aligned activity spinner, so spinner cells overlapping a chip remain clickable as config chips.
When the autocomplete popup falls back to centered placement over the prompt title, retained chip hitboxes still take precedence over the popup's selectable surface.
component_handles_mouse claims Drag and Up events over config chips, causing DashboardContext::route_selection to clear active transcript or prompt selections dragged across the prompt border.
attention_level returns Unreachable before checking for a failed review or failed forwarding, downgrading Failed below Unreachable.
notification_body has no arm for the new AttentionLevel::Unreachable, so unreachable worker notifications fall through to the last agent message or "Finished".
The wide minimized Sessions pane title omits the urgency glyph, rendering only "Attention: N" instead of identifying the most urgent level.
session_activity_line still checks facts.unreachable and facts.needs_input() instead of facts.attention, causing its status text to disagree with the reordered row glyph.
The new documentation promises that failed moves receive a Failed attention badge, but failed moves that leave the session Stopped classify as Inactive with no badge or prefix+o entry.
The new Muse model-catalog staging path has no test coverage, while the existing Muse discovery unit test was removed.
muse_data_dir compares the profile home lexically against own_home, so symlinked or relative paths aliasing the user's Muse home look under <home>/.data/muse and miss the saved catalog.
stage_profile checks catalog.exists(), which swallows permission or I/O errors when probing the Muse data directory and silently falls back to the built-in model.
Already-running Muse sessions do not receive the saved model catalog during worker binary upgrades because stage_profile is not called on upgrade.
The new 60-second prompt readiness wait does not hold an upgrade::activity permit, so an automatic daemon upgrade can shut down and drop a pending prompt.
A prompt arriving initially after the worker handshake marks state running but before the first operational report sets capabilities.prompt is immediately rejected with 409.
Breaking out of the readiness wait on capabilities.prompt alone races with pending startup follow-ups (model, effort, or initial prompt) and fails with 500.

Panicking on timeout or failure inside native_muse_turn skips closing and awaiting the spawned runtime task, so unwinding removes the caller's TempDir while the adapter and native Muse processes are still running.

supervise waits for both stdout and stderr pipe EOF before publishing the child's exit, stalling terminal/wait_for_exit and omitting exitStatus when a background descendant keeps a pipe open.
ProcessGroup::kill_if_live skips signaling the terminal's process group once the shell leader has exited, leaving surviving background descendants running after kill, release, or shutdown.
Reaping the shell leader inside tokio::join! while a detached descendant holds a pipe open leaves exit unset, allowing kill_if_live to later signal a reused PID/PGID.
Putting client terminals in their own process groups puts them outside bare-worker teardown, so killing the worker daemon leaves terminal commands running while their working files are deleted.
Client terminals inherit only the worker daemon environment plus request.env, omitting the configured session/profile environment from spec.environment.
TerminalRegistry::shutdown kills and awaits terminal supervisors serially with a 5-second timeout per terminal, causing teardown to scale linearly and delaying kills of subsequent terminals.
TerminalBuffer::read applies output_byte_limit before String::from_utf8_lossy expansion (and new(0) clamps to 1), allowing invalid UTF-8 output to exceed the requested byte cap by up to 3x.

TerminalRegistry restarts terminal IDs at term-1 after a worker restart or resume, causing new terminal outputs to overwrite historical tool-call outputs with the same ID in the transcript projection.
TerminalRegistry::output releases the buffer lock before reading exit, allowing a concurrent completion to pair stale output with a completed exitStatus.
Released terminals are removed from TerminalRegistry and detached via tokio::spawn, so connection shutdown can emit RuntimeEvent::Stopped before they finish reaping and sending TerminalClosed.
